paragraphs: Huron is a global professional services firm that partners with clients to put possible into practice by creating sound strategies, optimizing operations, accelerating digital transformation, and empowering businesses to own their future. By embracing diverse perspectives, encouraging new ideas and challenging the status quo, we create sustainable results for the organizations we serve.
We are headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, with additional locations in the United States and abroad in Canada, France, India, Poland, Singapore, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.

The combination of our deep industry expertise and breadth of our offerings is the foundation of our growth strategy and why our clients choose Huron as their trusted advisor. Key focus areas of our growth strategy include:

•Accelerating Growth in Healthcare and Education: Huron holds leading market positions in healthcare and education, providing comprehensive offerings to the largest health systems, academic medical centers, colleges and universities, and research institutes in the United States and abroad. The Company will continue to broaden its portfolio of offerings in healthcare and education to drive even greater impact on current and new clients as the needs in those industries further evolve due to competitive, regulatory, financial, and broader market changes.

•Growing Presence in Commercial Industries: Through its deep industry and capability expertise and nimble approach, Huron has grown its client base and expanded its credentials in the commercial industries. Huron's commercial industry focus has increased the diversification of the Company's portfolio and end markets while expanding the range of capabilities it can deliver to clients, providing new avenues for growth and an important balance to its healthcare and education focus.

•Rapidly Growing Global Digital Capability: As data, technology and artificial intelligence ("AI") evolve across industries, Huron's ability to provide a broad portfolio of digital offerings that support the strategic and operational needs of its clients globally is at the foundation of the Company's strategy. Huron will continue to advance its integrated digital platform to support its strong growth trajectory.

•Solid Foundation for Margin Expansion: The Company continues to be well-positioned to further achieve margin expansion as well as strong annual adjusted diluted earnings per share growth. We are committed to operating income margin expansion by growing the areas of the business that provide the most attractive returns, improving our pricing realization and the operational
efficiency of our delivery for clients, utilizing our global delivery platform across regions, and scaling our selling, general, and administrative expenses as we grow.

•Strong Balance Sheet and Cash Flows: A resilient, flexible balance sheet is the foundation of our financial strength, and strong free cash flows have and will continue to be the hallmark of Huron's business model. The Company is committed to deploying capital in a strategic and balanced way, including returning capital to shareholders and executing strategic, tuck-in acquisitions while prudently managing our leverage ratio.

We provide our services and products and manage our business under three operating segments - Healthcare, Education, and Commercial - which aligns our business by industry. The Commercial segment includes all industries outside of healthcare and education, including, but not limited to, financial services, industrials and manufacturing, energy and utilities, and the public sector. We also provide revenue reporting across two principal capabilities: i) Consulting and Managed Services and ii) Digital, which are methods by which we deliver our services and products.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we derived 50%, 30% and 20% of our consolidated revenues before reimbursable expenses from our Healthcare, Education and Commercial operating segments, respectively.

Our Healthcare segment serves acute care providers, including national and regional health systems; academic health systems; community health systems; the federal health system; and public, children's and critical access hospitals, and non-acute care providers, including physician practices and medical groups; payors; and long-term care or post-acute providers. Our healthcare-focused consulting and managed services offerings include financial and operational performance improvement consulting, which spans revenue cycle, business operations and care delivery transformation; organizational transformation; revenue cycle managed services and outsourcing; financial and capital advisory consulting; and strategy and innovation consulting. Our healthcare-focused digital services span technology and analytic-related services, including core systems of record, such as enterprise health record ("EHR"), enterprise resource planning ("ERP"), enterprise performance management ("EPM"), and customer relationship management ("CRM") systems; data management, AI and automation; technology managed services; and payor core administration systems. We also have a portfolio of software products we deliver to the healthcare industry. In June 2025, we enhanced our consulting offerings through the acquisition of Eclipse Insights LLC ("Eclipse Insights"), a leading provider of revenue cycle solutions. In November 2025, we acquired the consulting services division of AXIOM Systems Consulting Services, Inc. ("AXIOM") to strengthen our digital-focused payor offerings.

Our Education segment serves public and private colleges and universities, research institutes, not-for-profit organizations and other education-related organizations. Our education and research-focused consulting and managed services offerings include our research-focused consulting and managed services; our strategy and operations consulting services, which span finance, accounting, operations and athletics to organization and talent strategy and student and academic strategy; and our advancement and fundraising consulting services, which were bolstered by the acquisition of Grenzebach Glier and Associates ("GG+A") in March of 2024 and Advancement Resources and Halpin Parnership Limited ("Halpin") in March 2025. Our education and research-focused digital offerings span technology and analytic-related services, including core systems of record, such as student information, ERP, EPM, and CRM systems; data management, AI and automation; and technology managed services. Our education and research-focused product offerings include our Huron Research Suite, the leading software suite designed to facilitate and improve research administration service delivery and compliance.

Our Commercial segment is focused on serving industries and organizations facing significant disruption and regulatory change by helping them adapt to rapidly changing environments and accelerate business transformation. Our Commercial professionals work primarily with seven primary buyers: the chief executive officer, the chief financial officer, the chief strategy officer, the chief human resources officer, the chief operating officer, the chief risk officer, and organizational advisors, including lenders and law firms. We have a deep focus on serving organizations in the financial services, industrials and manufacturing, and energy and utilities industries and the public sector while opportunistically serving commercial industries more broadly, including professional and business services, life sciences, consumer products, and retail. headings: Risks Related to Human Capital Resources
An inability to retain our senior management team and managing directors and principals would be detrimental to the success of our business.
If we are unable to hire and retain talented people in an industry where there is great competition for talent, it could have a serious negative effect on our prospects and results of operations.
If we are unable to manage the organizational challenges associated with our continued growth, we might be unable to achieve our business objectives.
Risks Related to Business Operations, Growth and Development
We may incur costs to support our business and the inability to effectively build a support structure for the business could have an adverse impact on our growth and profitability.
Our international operations could result in additional risks.
The Company has significant operations in India, which presents additional risks.
Additional hiring, departures, and business acquisitions and dispositions, as well as other organizational changes, could disrupt our operations, increase our costs or otherwise harm our business.
The healthcare and education industries are areas of significant focus for our business, and factors that affect the financial condition of these industries could consequently affect our business.
Conflicts of interest could preclude us from accepting engagements thereby causing decreased utilization and revenues.
Our ability to maintain and attract new business depends upon our reputation, the professional reputation of our revenue-generating employees, and the quality of our services.
The consulting services industry is highly competitive and we may not be able to compete effectively.
Risks Related to Information Technology
Our business is becoming increasingly dependent on information technology and will require additional investments in order to grow and meet the demands of our clients.
Adverse changes to our relationships with key third-party vendors or the business of our key third-party vendors could unfavorably impact our business.
We could experience system failures, service interruptions, or security breaches that could negatively impact our business.
Issues related to the use of AI may result in reputational harm or liability that could adversely impact our business.
Risks Related to Legal Matters
Our reputation could be damaged and we could incur additional liabilities if we fail to protect client and employee data through our own accord or if our information systems are breached.
Our engagements could result in professional liability, which could be very costly and hurt our reputation.
Our business could be materially adversely affected if we incur liability in connection with service offering innovation, including new or expanded service offerings.
Our intellectual property rights in our "Huron Consulting Group" name are important, and any inability to use that name could negatively impact our ability to build brand identity.
Risks Related to Financial Management and Performance
Our financial results could suffer if we are unable to achieve or maintain adequate utilization and suitable billing rates for our consultants.
Our quarterly and annual results of operations have fluctuated in the past and may continue to fluctuate in the future as a result of certain factors, some of which may be outside of our control.
Revenues from our performance-based engagements are difficult to predict, and the timing and extent of recovery of our costs is uncertain.
The profitability of our fixed-fee engagements with clients may not meet our expectations if we underestimate the cost of these engagements.
Our business performance might not be sufficient for us to meet the full-year financial guidance that we provide publicly.

paragraphs: The following discussion of risk factors may be important to understanding the statements in this Annual Report on Form 10-K or elsewhere. The following information should be read in conjunction with Part II—Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and the Consolidated Financial Statements and related notes in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Discussions about the important operational risks that our business encounters can be found in Part II—Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations."

We rely heavily on our senior management team, our industry and capability leaders, and managing directors and principals, and our ability to retain them is particularly important to our future success. Given the highly specialized nature of our services, the senior management team must have a thorough understanding of our service offerings as well as the skills and experience necessary to manage an organization consisting of a diverse group of professionals. In addition, we rely on our senior management team and managing directors and principals to generate revenues and market our business. Further, our senior management's and managing directors' and principals' personal reputations and relationships with our clients are a critical element in obtaining and maintaining client engagements. Members of our senior management team and our managing directors and principals could choose to leave or join one of our competitors and some of our clients could choose to use the services of that competitor instead of our services. If one or more members of our senior management team or our managing directors or principals leave and we cannot replace them with a suitable candidate quickly, or if legal restrictions on non-competition agreements are put into place, we could experience difficulty in securing and successfully completing engagements, managing our business properly and executing on our growth strategy, which could harm our business prospects and results of operations.

Our business involves the delivery of professional services and is highly labor-intensive. Our success depends largely on our general ability to attract, develop, motivate, and retain highly skilled professionals. Further, we must successfully maintain the right mix of professionals with relevant experience and skill sets as we continue to grow, as we expand into new service offerings, and as the market evolves. The loss of a significant number of our professionals, the inability to attract, hire, develop, train, and retain additional skilled personnel, or failure to maintain the right mix of professionals could have a serious negative effect on us, including our ability to manage, staff, and successfully complete our existing engagements and obtain new engagements. Further, if we cannot develop, train, and retain highly skilled professionals, it may impact our ability to keep pace with rapid and continuing changes in technology and respond to changes in client demand in a rapidly evolving market for professional services. Qualified professionals are in great demand, and we face significant competition for both senior and junior professionals with the requisite credentials and experience. Our principal competition for talent comes from other consulting firms and accounting firms, as well as from organizations seeking to staff their internal professional positions. Many of these competitors may be able to offer greater compensation and benefits or more attractive lifestyle choices, career paths, or geographic locations than we can offer. Additionally, we may find it difficult to hire, develop and retain qualified professionals in certain geographic regions where historically our operations have been limited. Therefore, we may not be successful in attracting and retaining the skilled consultants we require to conduct and expand our operations successfully. Increasing competition for these revenue-generating professionals may also significantly increase our labor costs, which could negatively affect our margins and results of operations.

As we continue to grow and evolve, it might become increasingly difficult to maintain effective standards across a large, global enterprise and effectively institutionalize our knowledge or to effectively change the strategy, operations or culture of our Company in a timely manner. It might also become more difficult to maintain our culture; effectively manage and monitor our people and operations; effectively communicate our core values, policies and procedures, strategies and goals; and motivate, engage and retain our people, particularly given the distribution of our employees across the U.S. and internationally, the rate of new hires, the breadth of skills and expertise across all of our solutions, and the fact that essentially all of our employees have the option to work remotely. The size and scope of our operations increase the possibility that we will have employees who expose us to unacceptable business risks, despite our efforts to train them and maintain internal controls to prevent such instances. For example, employee misconduct could involve the improper use of sensitive or confidential information entrusted to us, or obtained inappropriately, or the failure to comply with legislation or regulations regarding the protection of sensitive or confidential information, including personal data and proprietary information. Furthermore, the inappropriate use of social networking sites or AI by our employees could result in breaches of confidentiality, unauthorized disclosure of nonpublic company information or damage to our reputation. If we do not continue to develop and implement the right processes and tools to manage our enterprise and instill our culture and core values into all of our employees, our ability to compete successfully and achieve our business objectives could be impaired. In addition, effective

January 1, 2022, we made, and continue to make, changes to our operating model, including how we are organized as the needs and size of our business change, and despite the operating model yielding positive synergies and impacts to date, if we do not continue to successfully refine the changes, our business and results of operations may be negatively impacted.

We have grown significantly since we commenced operations and have increased the number of our full-time professionals from 249 in 2002 to approximately 8,610 as of December 31, 2025. Additionally, our considerable growth has placed demands on our management and our internal systems, procedures, and controls and will continue to do so in the future. To successfully manage growth, we must periodically adjust and strengthen our operating, financial, accounting, and other systems, procedures, compliance practices and controls, which may increase our total costs and may adversely affect our operating income and our ability to sustain profitability if we do not generate increased revenues to offset the costs. As a public company, our information and control systems must enable us to prepare accurate and timely financial information and other required disclosures. If we discover deficiencies in our existing information and control systems that impede our ability to satisfy our reporting requirements, we must successfully implement improvements to those systems in an efficient and timely manner.

paragraphs: Highlights from the year ended December 31, 2025 include the following:
•Revenues before reimbursable expenses increased 11.9% to $1.66 billion in 2025 from $1.49 billion in 2024.

•Net income as a percentage of total revenues was 6.2% in 2025, compared to 7.7% in 2024. Results for 2025 include $7.7 million of non-cash impairment charges, net of tax, related to our convertible debt investment in a third-party. Results for 2024 include an $11.1 million litigation settlement gain, net of tax, related to a completed legal matter in which Huron was the plaintiff.
•Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of revenues before reimbursable expenses increased to 14.3% in 2025 from 13.5% in 2024.

•Diluted EPS was $5.84 for 2025, compared to $6.27 for 2024. Results for 2025 include the non-cash impairment charge related to our convertible debt investment in a third-party, which had an unfavorable $0.43 impact on diluted earnings per share for the year. Results for 2024 include the litigation settlement gain related to a completed legal matter in which Huron was the plaintiff, which had a favorable impact of $0.60 on diluted earnings per share in 2024.
•Adjusted diluted EPS increased 21.0% to $7.83 for 2025, compared to $6.47 for 2024.
•Returned $166.2 million to shareholders by repurchasing 1,166,077 shares of our common stock in 2025.

Revenues before reimbursable expenses increased $176.8 million, or 11.9%, to $1.66 billion for the year ended December 31, 2025 from $1.49 billion for the year ended December 31, 2024. The overall increase in revenues before reimbursable expenses reflects strength in demand for our Consulting and Managed Services capabilities within all three of our segments, as well as continued strength in demand for our Digital capabilities within our Commercial and Education segments. The increase includes $86.0 million of incremental revenues before reimbursable expenses from our acquisitions completed since December 31, 2023. These increases were partially offset by a decrease in demand for our Digital capability within our Healthcare segment. Excluding the $86.0 million of incremental revenues before reimbursable expenses from our acquisitions and $13.7 million of revenues before reimbursable expenses in 2024 generated by the Studer Education business, which we divested at the end of 2024, revenues before reimbursable expenses grew 7.1% organically.

Revenues before reimbursable expenses within our Consulting and Managed Services capability increased 13.1% to $976.9 million in 2025, compared to $863.9 million in 2024; and reflected strengthened demand in all three of our segments. The increase includes $38.2 million of incremental revenues before reimbursable expenses from our acquisitions of Eclipse Insights, Treliant, Advancement Resources, WP&C, GG+A and Halpin. The utilization rate within our Consulting capability increased to 75.7% in 2025, compared to 73.6% in 2024.

Revenues before reimbursable expenses within our Digital capability increased 10.2% to $686.0 million in 2025, compared to $622.2 million in 2024; and reflected strengthened demand in our Commercial and Education segments, partially offset by a decrease in demand in our Healthcare segment. The increase includes $47.8 million of incremental revenues before reimbursable expenses from our acquisitions of AXIA Consulting, Inc ("AXIA Consulting") and AXIOM. The utilization rate within our Digital capability increased to 78.2% in 2025, compared to 76.0% in 2024.

Our total number of revenue-generating professionals, excluding Managed Services professionals, increased 13.1% to 5,307 as of December 31, 2025, compared to 4,694 as of December 31, 2024, as a result of the acquisitions completed since December 31, 2024 and hiring to support the overall increase in demand for our services. The number of Managed Services professionals increased 46.3% to 2,239 as of December 31, 2025 from 1,530 as of December 31, 2024. We proactively plan and manage the size and composition of our workforce and take actions as needed to address changes in the anticipated demand for our services as employee compensation costs are the most significant portion of our operating expenses.

Net income decreased $11.6 million, or 9.9%, to $105.0 million, or 6.2% of total revenues, for the year ended December 31, 2025 from $116.6 million, or 7.7% of total revenues, for the same period last year. Results for 2025 include $7.7 million of non-cash impairment charges, net of tax, related to our convertible debt investment in a third-party. Results for 2024 include an $11.1 million litigation settlement gain, net of tax, related to a completed legal matter in which Huron was the plaintiff. As a result of the decrease in net income, and partially offset by a reduction in diluted shares outstanding resulting from share repurchases made under our share repurchase plan, diluted earnings per share decreased 6.9% to $5.84 for 2025, compared to $6.27 for 2024. Adjusted diluted earnings per share, which excludes the impact of the non-cash impairment charges in 2025 and the litigation settlement gain in 2024, increased 21.0% to $7.83 for 2025 from $6.47 for 2024.

Adjusted EBITDA increased $36.3 million, or 18.1%, to $237.5 million, or 14.3% of revenues before reimbursable expenses, in 2025, compared to $201.2 million, or 13.5% of revenues before reimbursable expenses, in 2024.
During 2025, we deployed $166.2 million of capital to repurchase 1,166,077 shares of our common stock, representing 6.6% of our common stock outstanding as of December 31, 2024.

paragraphs: Huron 是一家全球專業服務機構，與客戶合作將可能的方案付諸實踐，透過制定健全的策略、優化作業、加速數位轉型，並賦能企業掌握自己的未來。透過擁抱多元觀點、鼓勵新思維並挑戰現狀，我們為所服務的組織創造可持續的成果。
本公司總部設於美國伊利諾州芝加哥，並在美國及其他國家如加拿大、法國、印度、波蘭、新加坡、瑞士及英國設有分部。
我們深厚的產業專業知識與廣泛的產品組合，是我們成長策略的基礎，也是客戶選擇 Huron 作為他們信賴顧問的原因。我們成長策略的主要著重領域包括：
•加速醫療與教育領域的成長：Huron 在醫療與教育領域擁有領先的市場地位，為美國及海外最大的醫療系統、教學醫院、大學與學院以及研究機構提供全面的解決方案。本公司將持續擴充在醫療與教育領域的產品組合，以因應這些產業因競爭、法規、財務及更廣泛市場變動而進一步演進的需要，為現有及新客戶帶來更大的影響。
•在商業產業的擴張成長：透過其深厚的產業與能力專業知識以及靈活的作風，Huron 已擴大其客戶羣並在商業產業中提升其聲譽。Huron 對商業產業的專注，已增加本公司的產品組合與終端市場的多元化，同時擴展其能為客戶提供的能力範圍，提供新的成長途徑，並為其醫療與教育的重點提供重要的平衡。
•快速成長的全球數位能力：隨著數據、科技與人工智慧（"AI"）在各產業中持續演進，Huron 提供廣泛的數位產品組合，以支持其客戶在全球範圍內的戰略與運營需求，這是本公司策略的基礎。Huron 將持續進步其整合的數位平台，以支持其強勁的成長軌跡。
•穩固的獲利擴張基礎：本公司持續處於有利位置，以進一步實現獲利擴張以及強勁的年度調整後稀釋每股盈餘成長。我們致力於透過擴大提供最吸引人回報的業務領域、改善我們的定價實現度與為客戶提供的運營效率，利用我們的全球交付平台在各區域進行運作，並在成長過程中控制我們的營銷、一般及行政費用。
•提升運營效率：本公司持續處於有利位置，以進一步實現獲利擴張以及強勁的年度調整後稀釋每股盈餘成長。我們致力於透過擴大提供最吸引人回報的業務領域、改善我們的定價實現度與為客戶提供的運營效率，利用我們的全球交付平台在各區域進行運作，並在成長過程中控制我們的營銷、一般及行政費用。
•強固的資產負債表與現金流：一個強韌且靈活的資產負債表是我們財務強勢的基礎，且強勁的自由現金流一直是 Huron 商業模式的特徵。本公司致力於以戰略且平衡的方式運用資本，包括回饋股東以及執行戰略性的收購，同時謹慎管理我們的負債比率。
我們提供服務與產品並經營業務於三個運營分部 - 醫療、教育與商業 - 這與產業對齊。商業分部包含所有非醫療與教育產業，包括但不限於金融服務、工業與製造、能源與公用事業以及公部門。我們也透過兩種主要能力提供收入報表：i) 諮詢與管理服務，以及 ii) 數位化，這是我們提供服務與產品的方法。
截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們來自醫療、教育與商業運營分部的合併營業收入（扣除可報銷費用前）分別佔總營業收入的 50%、30% 和 20%。

我們的醫療分部服務急診照護提供者，包括國家與區域性醫療系統；學術醫療系統；社區醫療系統；聯邦醫療系統；以及公共、兒童與急症照護醫院，以及非急診照護提供者，包括醫生診所與醫療集團；保險機構；以及長期照護或後續照護提供者。我們專注於醫療的諮詢與管理服務，包括財務與運營績效改善諮詢，涵蓋收入週期、業務運作與照護交付轉型；組織轉型；收入週期管理服務與委外；財務與資本諮詢；以及策略與創新諮詢。我們專注於醫療的數位服務涵蓋科技與分析相關服務，包括核心系統，如企業健康記錄（"EHR"）、企業資源規劃（"ERP"）、企業績效管理（"EPM"）以及客戶關係管理（"CRM"）系統；數據管理、人工智能與自動化；科技管理服務；以及保險核心行政系統。我們也擁有軟體產品組合，提供給醫療產業。2025 年 6 月，我們透過收購 Eclipse Insights LLC（"Eclipse Insights"），一家領先的收入週期解決方案供應商，強化了我們的諮詢服務。2025 年 11 月，我們收購了 AXIOM Systems Consulting Services, Inc.（"AXIOM"）的諮詢服務部門，以強化我們專注於數位化的保險機構服務。

我們的教育分部服務公立與私立大學、研究機構、非營利組織及其他教育相關機構。我們的教育與研究專注諮詢與管理服務包括我們的專注於研究的諮詢與管理服務；我們的策略與運營諮詢服務，涵蓋財務、會計、運營與體育到組織與人才策略以及學生與學術策略；以及我們的推廣與募款諮詢服務，這部分因 2024 年 3 月收購 Grenzebach Glier and Associates（"GG+A"）以及 2025 年 3 月收購 Advancement Resources and Halpin Parnership Limited（"Halpin"）而得到強化。我們的教育與研究專注數位服務涵蓋科技與分析相關服務，包括核心系統，如學生資訊、ERP、EPM 以及 CRM 系統；數據管理、人工智能與自動化；以及科技管理服務。我們的教育與研究專注產品服務包括 Huron Research Suite，這是一套領先的軟體組合，用以促進並改善研究行政服務的交付與合規性。

我們的商業分部專注於服務面臨重大變動與規範變更的產業與機構，協助他們適應快速變化的環境並加速業務轉型。我們的商業專業人員主要與七個主要買家合作：首席執行官、首席財務官、首席策略官、首席人力資源官、首席運營官、首席風險官以及組織顧問，包括貸款機構與律師事務所。我們對服務金融服務、工業與製造以及能源與公用事業產業以及公部門有深入的關注，同時機會性地服務更廣泛的商業產業，包括專業與商業服務、生命科學、消費產品與零售。我們的商業專業人員運用其深厚的產業、功能與技術專業知識，提供我們的數位服務與軟體產品、財務與資本諮詢（特殊情況諮詢與企業財務諮詢）服務、規範合規與風險管理諮詢與管理

paragraphs: 2025 年截至 12 月 31 日的年度重點包含以下內容：
•扣除可報銷費用前的營業收入增加 11.9%，至 2025 年的 1.66 十億美元，較 2024 年的 1.49 十億美元成長。
•營業收入的淨利潤率為 6.2%（2025 年），較 2024 年的 7.7% 下降。2025 年的結果包含 7.7 百萬美元的非現金減值費用（稅後淨額），與本公司對第三方的可轉換債務投資有關。2024 年的結果包含 11.1 百萬美元的訴訟和解獲利（稅後淨額），與 Huron 為原告的已完成法律事務有關。
•扣除可報銷費用前的調整後營業現金流（Adjusted EBITDA）佔營業收入的比例增至 2025 年的 14.3%，較 2024 年的 13.5% 上升。
•稀釋後每股盈餘為 2025 年的 5.84 美元，較 2024 年的 6.27 美元下降。2025 年的結果包含與本公司對第三方的可轉換債務投資有關的非現金減值費用，對該年度稀釋後每股盈餘產生不利影響 0.43 美元。2024 年的結果包含與 Huron 為原告的已完成法律事務有關的訴訟和解獲利，對該年度稀釋後每股盈餘產生有利影響 0.60 美元。
•稀釋後每股盈餘（調整後）增加 21.0%，至 2025 年的 7.83 美元，較 2024 年的 6.47 美元成長。
•2025 年透過回購 1,166,077 股本公司普通股，回饋給股東 166.2 百萬美元。

扣除可報銷費用前的營業收入增加 176.8 百萬美元，或成長 11.9%，至 2025 年截至 12 月 31 日的 1.66 十億美元，較 2024 年截至 12 月 31 日的 1.49 十億美元成長。扣除可報銷費用前營業收入的總體成長反映各應報告分部中諮詢與 Managed Services 能力的需求強勁，以及商業與教育分部中數位能力的需求持續強勁。成長包含自 2023 年 12 月 31 日後完成的收購所產生的 86.0 百萬美元扣除可報銷費用前營業收入。這些成長部分抵銷了醫療分部中數位能力需求下降的影響。扣除收購所產生的 86.0 百萬美元扣除可報銷費用前營業收入，以及 2024 年由 Studer 教育業務產生的 13.7 百萬美元扣除可報銷費用前營業收入（該業務於 2024 年底已出售），扣除可報銷費用前營業收入的有機成長為 7.1%。

我們 Digital 服務能力中，扣除可報銷費用的營業收入增加 10.2% 至 686 百萬美元，在 2025 年，較 2024 年的 622.2 百萬美元；並反映我們 Commercial 與 Education 分部需求強化，部分抵銷 Healthcare 分部需求減少。此增加包含來自我們收購 AXIA Consulting, Inc ("AXIA Consulting") 及 AXIOM 所產生的 47.8 百萬美元扣除可報銷費用的增量收入。我們 Digital 服務能力的使用率在 2025 年增加至 78.2%，較 2024 年的 76.0%。

我們扣除 Managed Services 專業人員的營收產生專業人員總數增加 13.1% 至 5,307 人，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 4,694 人，係因自 2024 年 12 月 31 日後完成的收購及為支持我們服務需求增加而進行的招募。Managed Services 專業人員數量增加 46.3% 至 2,239 人，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日的 1,530 人。我們會主動規劃及管理員工規模與組成，並根據預期服務需求變動，必要時採取行動以應對員工薪資成本為我們營運費用中最大的部分。

淨利減少 11.6 百萬美元，或 9.9%，至 105 百萬美元，為總營收的 6.2%，在 2025 年 12 月 31 日結帳年度，較 2024 年同期的 116.6 百萬美元，為總營收的 7.7%。2025 年結果包含 7.7 百萬美元的非現金減值費用，扣除稅後，與我們對第三方的可轉換債務投資有關。2024 年結果包含 11.1 百萬美元的訴訟和解獲利，扣除稅後，與 Huron 為原告的已完成法律事項有關。由於淨利減少，並部分抵銷因根據我們股票回購計畫所進行的股票回購導致流通股數減少，每股經稀釋的盈餘減少 6.9% 至 5.84 美元，較 2024 年的 6.27 美元。調整後每股經稀釋盈餘，排除 2025 年非現金減值費用及 2024 年訴訟和解獲利的影響，增加 21.0% 至 7.83 美元，較 2024 年的 6.47 美元。
調整後 EBITDA 增加 36.3 百萬美元，或 18.1%，至 237.5 百萬美元，為扣除可報銷費用營業收入的 14.3%，在 2025 年，較 2024 年的 201.2 百萬美元，為扣除可報銷費用營業收入的 13.5%。
在 2025 年，我們投入 166.2 百萬美元資本，回購 1,166,077 張我們普通股，代表截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日普通股發行在外數量的 6.6%。

headings: 與人力資源相關的風險
無法留住我們的高階管理團隊及 managing directors 和 principals 將對本公司業務的成功造成不利影響。
若我們無法在人才競爭激烈的產業中聘請並留住優秀人才，將可能對本公司前景及營運結果產生嚴重負面影響。
若我們無法管理與持續成長相關的組織挑戰，可能會無法達成本公司業務目標。
與業務運作、成長及發展相關的風險
本公司可能產生支應業務的費用，且無法有效建立支援業務的架構，將可能對本公司成長及獲利能力產生不利影響。
本公司國際業務可能產生額外風險。
本公司在印度有顯著業務運作，這會產生額外風險。
額外的僱用、離職、業務收購與處分，以及其他組織變動，可能幹擾我們的營運，增加我們的成本，或以其他方式損害我們的業務。
醫療與教育產業是我們業務的重要關注領域，影響這些產業財務狀況的因素，可能會進而影響我們的業務。
利益衝突可能使我們無法接受委託，因而導致利用率與收入下降。
我們維持並吸引新業務的能力，取決於我們的聲譽、營收產生員工的專業聲譽，以及我們服務的品質。
諮詢服務產業競爭激烈，我們可能無法有效競爭。
與資訊科技相關的風險
我們的業務正變得越來越依賴資訊科技，並將需要額外的投資，以實現成長並符合客戶的需求。
我們與關鍵第三方供應商的關係惡化，或這些關鍵第三方供應商的業務出現不利變動，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們可能遭遇系統故障、服務中斷或安全漏洞，這可能會對我們的業務造成負面影響。
與AI使用相關的問題可能會導致聲譽損害或法律責任，這可能會對我們的業務造成不利影響。
與法律事務相關的風險
如果我們未能透過自身努力保護客戶及員工資料，或我們的資訊系統遭入侵，可能會導致聲譽受損，並產生額外的責任。
我們的業務可能會因專業責任而產生高昂成本，並損害我們的聲譽。
如果我們因服務創新而產生責任，包括新或擴展的服務項目，可能會對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。
我們在 "Huron Consulting Group" 名稱上的智慧財產權非常重要，若無法使用該名稱，可能會對我們建立品牌識別度的能力造成負面影響。
與財務管理及營運績效相關的風險
本公司財務結果若無法達成或維持諮詢師的充足利用率及合適計費率，可能會受到影響。
本公司過去的季度及年度營運結果曾出現波動，未來也可能因某些因素而繼續出現波動，其中一些因素可能超出本公司控制範圍。
本公司以績效為基礎的服務合約所產生的收入較難預測，且本公司成本的回收時間與程度亦存在不確定性。
本公司與客戶簽訂的固定費用合約之獲利情況，若低估這些合約的成本，可能無法達到本公司預期。
本公司營運表現可能不足以使本公司達成公開提供的全年財務指引。

paragraphs: {'translated_text': '以下風險因素的討論可能對理解本年度報表 10-K 或其他地方的陳述具有重要性。以下資訊應與本年度報表 10-K 第二部分—第 7 項 "管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析" 以及合併財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。有關我們業務所面臨的重要營運風險之討論，可見於第二部分—第 7 項 "管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析"。'}

{'translated_text': '我們高度依賴我們的高階管理團隊、產業與能力領導者、管理董事與主要股東，我們能否留住他們對我們未來的成功至關重要。考慮到我們服務的高專業性，高階管理團隊必須對我們的服務內容有深入的瞭解，並具備管理一個由多樣化專業人士組成組織所需的技能與經驗。此外，我們依賴高階管理團隊與管理董事與主要股東來產生收入並行銷我們的業務。進一步而言，我們高階管理人員與管理董事與主要股東的個人聲譽與與客戶的關係，是取得與維持客戶委託的重要因素。我們高階管理團隊與管理董事與主要股東有可能選擇離開或加入我們的競爭對手，而部分客戶也可能選擇使用該競爭對手的服務而非我們的服務。若有一名或多名高階管理團隊或管理董事與主要股東離開，而我們無法迅速找到合適的候選人取代，或若非競爭協議的法律限制被實施，我們可能會在取得並成功完成委託、妥善管理業務與執行成長策略上遇到困難，這可能會影響我們的業務前景與營運結果。'}

{'translated_text': '我們的業務涉及專業服務的提供，屬於高度勞動密集型。我們的成功在很大程度上取決於我們吸引、培養、激勵與留住高技能專業人才的一般能力。此外，我們必須成功維持適當的專業人才組合，這些人才具備相關經驗與技能，以應對我們持續成長、擴展至新服務項目以及市場演進的過程。失去大量專業人才、無法吸引、招聘、培養、訓練與留住更多技能人才，或未能維持適當的專業人才組合，可能對我們造成嚴重的負面影響，包括我們管理、配置人力與成功完成現有委託的能力，以及取得新委託的能力。進一步而言，若我們無法培養、訓練與留住高技能專業人才，可能會影響我們跟上技術快速且持續的變革，並對客戶需求的變化做出迅速反應的能力。具備資格的專業人才需求極高，我們在高階與低階專業人才的招募上面臨極大的競爭。我們在人才招募的主要競爭對手來自其他顧問公司與會計公司，以及尋求內部專業職位的人力資源機構。這些競爭對手可能能提供更高的薪資與福利、更吸引人的生活方式選擇、職業發展路徑或地理位置。此外，我們可能在某些地理區域遇到困難，這些區域過去我們的業務活動較有限。因此，我們可能無法成功吸引並留住執行我們業務與擴展業務所需的專業人才。這些產生收入的專業人才的競爭增加，也可能大幅提高我們的勞動成本，這可能會對我們的毛利率與營運結果產生負面影響。'}

{'translated_text': '隨著我們持續成長與演進，維持一個大型全球企業的有效標準，並有效將知識制度化，或有效調整公司的策略、營運或文化，可能變得越來越困難。同時，維持我們的企業文化、有效管理與監督我們的員工與營運、有效傳達我們的核心價值觀、政策與程序、策略與目標，以及激勵、參與與留住我們的員工，也變得更加困難，特別是考慮到我們員工分佈於美國與國際間、新進員工的比率、我們所有解決方案中廣泛的技能與專業知識，以及我們幾乎所有員工都有選擇遠端工作的權利。我們的規模與範疇增加，使我們有更多員工可能對我們造成不可接受的業務風險，儘管我們努力培訓他們並維持內部控制以防止這些情況發生。例如，員工的不當行為可能涉及對我們委託的敏感或機密資訊的不當使用，或未經授權取得的資訊，或未遵守保護敏感或機密資訊的法律與法規，包括個人資訊與專有資訊。此外，員工不當使用社交媒體網站或人工智慧，可能導致機密資訊外洩、未經授權揭露非公開公司資訊或損害我們的聲譽。若我們未能持續發展與實施正確的流程與工具來管理企業並將我們的企業文化與核心價值觀植入所有員工，我們在競爭中成功並達成業務目標的能力可能會受到影響。此外，有效的'}
{'translated_text': '2022 年 1 月 1 日，我們進行並持續進行經營模式的調整，包括根據業務需求與規模的變化而調整我們的組織結構，儘管目前的經營模式已產生正面的協同效益與影響，若我們未能持續成功優化這些調整，我們的業務與營運結果可能會受到負面影響。'}

{'translated_text': '自我們開始營運以來，我們已大幅成長，並將全職專業人才人數從 2002 年的 249 人增加至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的約 8,610 人。此外，我們的快速成長已對我們的管理與內部系統、程序與控制措施產生壓力，未來也會持續如此。為成功管理成長，我們必須定期調整與強化我們的營運、財務、會計及其他系統、程序、合規實踐與控制措施，這可能會增加我們的總成本，並可能對我們的營運收入與維持利潤能力產生負面影響，若我們無法產生更高的收入來彌補這些成本。作為上市公司，我們的資訊與控制系統必須能協助我們準備準確且及時的財務資訊及其他所需披露資料。若我們發現現有資訊與控制系統的缺陷，影響我們滿足報告要求的能力，我們必須成功在高效且及時的時間內實施這些系統的改進。'}
